title: Report previous, current, and per-round progress beside visual percentage bars
abstract: When reporting measurable progress on an active project or roadmap item, pair its visual completion bar with three explicitly labeled values: the verified completion percentage before this reporting round, the verified completion percentage after this round, and the net percentage-point change during this round (after minus before). Use a consistent item, scope and acceptance-criteria denominator for the comparison. Show zero change when no measurable advancement occurred and a negative change if a corrected estimate declines. If an earlier baseline or defensible completion estimate is unavailable, say it is unknown rather than inventing numbers; do not portray a visually filled bar or repeated status as evidence of work.

source.reference: Generalized relative-progress visual reporting requirement; no private conversation wording retained

scope_hints.scope_boundary: Progress reports for active projects and relevant unfinished roadmap items when a defensible, comparable completion percentage is available. The 'round' means work since the preceding verified progress report for the same item. Applies to overall project progress when reported, too. This complements rather than changes existing visual-bar and completion-evidence requirements. Do not create an artificial completion denominator or falsely assert percentage gains when only activity is known.

unresolved: During normalization, specify a consistent presentation for unavailable before/after values, without ever inventing a percentage.
Confirm the treatment of downward progress corrections and whether 'change' should be signed in percentage points in all reporting surfaces.
remarks: Queued as an independent increment to existing visual progress reporting rules. No canonical rule created or activated.
